changelog: v2 principle: a reject needs reliable identity, i.e. a corpus-listed committee. Every other conflict signal (an ancestor, an unlisted name, a proceeding name) can only make the answer qualified, never supported.

R7 (amends R5): a proceeding or classless setting never rejects on an ancestor. An ancestor naming a different proceeding, or a specific body of another kind, gives qualified. A same or generic ancestor passes.

R8: committee identity is read at the leaf-most committee segment, even when that segment is an ancestor. A different listed body there rejects. Conflicting same-kind segments give qualified. A same-body match whose leaf is cross-kind gives qualified, in both directions.

R9: the Committee of the whole House is its own sub-kind. A plain House or Chamber setting against a Committee-of-the-whole leaf or chapter is qualified, and so is the reverse. Committee of the whole against itself matches.
R10: a bare 'in committee' is qualified against a select committee or the Committee of the whole, never withheld.
R11: an unlisted name against a listed body, a cross-kind homonym, a proceeding against a specific committee, and a named hearing against a same-named inquiry are all qualified.

R12: whole words after macron folding only. A different proceeding head is qualified. General headings ('... IN GENERAL') are generic and pass. Identical unlisted names match on equality. A House debate whose leaf mentions committees stays qualified.
Deferred: rows tagged deferred='batch 2' (selector-route act attestation) are kept in the file but excluded from pass rates.
R13 (amends R1/R3/R8 for committee settings): a committee setting against a generic House-level leaf (e.g. a sittings or adjournment-of-the-House heading) is qualified, not withheld.

R13: a reject remains only for a listed committee against a Committee-of-the-whole leaf, a listed committee against a specific House proceeding, or a listed body against a different listed body (R3, R8). An unlisted or generic committee phrase against a Committee-of-the-whole leaf is qualified.

R13 confirmations (no outcome change): a subcommittee against its parent committee is qualified; a Committee-of-the-whole setting against an unlisted body is qualified; 'in committee' against the Committee of the whole's own rules is qualified.

R14: a 'specific House proceeding' means a proceeding named in the corpus only. A listed committee against a House setting that names a proceeding phrase not in the corpus is qualified, not withheld: a phrase outside the corpus cannot reject. A generic proceeding phrase against a same-kind leaf still passes (S-115 stays supported).

R15: a bare 'Debate' leaf is a generic, House-family proceeding. A House or Chamber setting passes against it uncapped (supported), unless another conflict signal (a specific committee or a Committee-of-the-whole chapter in the path) applies.
FR16: rule R14 does not exempt proper-noun ancestors from R7. A classless setting that matches its leaf is qualified when an ancestor names a different specific body or a different proceeding.

FR17: an ancestor caps a classless setting only when it carries an identity signal: a listed body, a corpus proceeding, the Committee of the whole, a committee-shaped name, or a committee chapter or part. Generic content words in an ancestor never cap. A setting equal to its own leaf is uncapped under generic ancestors.

FR19: a House or Chamber setting passes uncapped (supported) against a House-level leaf, even when an ancestor names a listed body. A Committee-of-the-whole leaf or chapter is still not House-level (R9).

FR13 (text of the R13 rule, unchanged in effect): a subcommittee against its parent committee is qualified. A committee setting against a generic House-level leaf (a sittings or adjournment-of-the-House heading) is qualified. Withheld applies only to a listed committee against a Committee-of-the-whole leaf, against a specific corpus House proceeding, or against a different listed body.

FR18: a name identifies a listed body only when its content tokens match that body uniquely. Short, partial or prefix-only names that fit more than one body, or none, are unlisted. Unlisted against listed is qualified, never supported or withheld. Stripping a heading prefix never turns a remaining name into a generic one.

FR20 (FR16 prevails over FR17): a classless setting that equals its own leaf is immune to generic ancestors only. An ancestor that carries an identity signal (a listed body, a corpus proceeding, the Committee of the whole, a committee-shaped name, or a committee chapter or part) and differs from the setting gives qualified. The FR8 reject applies only to committee settings against a different listed body. Identity class is the signal; word count never is (the one-word sub-rule is withdrawn).
FR19 (confirmed): a House or Chamber setting passes uncapped against a House-level leaf even under a listed-body ancestor. Committee-of-the-whole leaves and chapters are excluded (FR9).

FR21: a committee name is generic only when it has no content tokens beyond determiners ('the', 'a', 'any', 'this', ...) and the head word 'committee'. Any other name is listed when it uniquely equals one corpus record, and otherwise unlisted (qualified). The number of records a short form could fit does not matter: 'the Harbour Committee' and 'the review committee' are unlisted.

Identity rule (ruling 4): names are compared as whole words after NFC, case and macron folding only. There is no plural or stem folding, so 'Committee on Lanterns' does not match 'Lantern Committee'. A word-order variant matches only when the folded token multisets are identical.

FR21 class-word refinement: the committee-class words are the corpus category words MINUS every word that appears in a listed body's name. A category word that is also part of a listed name is never generic. Example: if 'Harbour' were a category word and 'Harbour Rules Committee' were listed, then 'the Harbour Committee' would be an unlisted short form, qualified against every listed body including 'Harbour Rules Committee' itself. For a fixture, the subtraction uses that fixture's own committee list.

FR18 (confirmed): a short form that is a proper subset of a listed name is qualified, even against the body it is a subset of. The only route to listed identity is exact equality of word multisets after function words are removed.

FR21 (clarified): a committee name is generic when every word in it is a determiner, the head word 'committee' or 'committees', a committee-class word, or one of the reference words {relevant, appropriate, responsible, same}. Committee-class words are the words the corpus itself uses to name categories of committees (the modifiers before a plural 'committees' in a structural heading). They are generated from the pinned corpus, not hand-listed. Any other word is content: 'the review committee' and 'the harbour committee' are not generic.

Identity rule (clarified): before the word-multiset comparison, function words (on, of, for, and, the, and determiners) are removed. So 'Committee on Lantern Affairs' matches 'Lantern Affairs Committee'. Plural differences still do not match: 'Lanterns Committee' does not match 'Lantern Committee'.
FR20 (confirmed): an ancestor that names the setting, including inside a combined heading ('FERNGULLY AND QUARRYSIDE' for 'the Ferngully'), does not differ from it.
No plural folding applies to names only. Recognising a proceeding kind may fold number: a 'Hearings' heading is the generic heading for 'hearing'.
FR20 applies to classless settings only. Settings with a proceeding class follow R7. A classless setting under a different listed body is qualified, not withheld.

FR22: a generic committee name (for example 'a committee' or 'the relevant committee') against a leaf that names a specific committee, whether listed or committee-shaped, is qualified. A generic name still passes against a generic or neutral committee leaf (for example a 'Select committees' heading or a general 'Committees' heading).

Confirmed: a singular or plural variant of a listed name ('Lanterns Committee' for 'Lantern Committee') is unlisted, which gives qualified. A reordered exact name ('Committee on Lantern Affairs' for 'Lantern Affairs Committee', after function words are removed) is listed: it matches its own body and is withheld against a different listed body.
Class words (confirmed source): committee-class words come only from structural headings that end in 'committees', never from body text, minus listed-name words. The pinned corpus yields no others.

FR20 (list closed): the identity signals that cap a classless self-match are exactly a listed body, a corpus proceeding, the Committee of the whole, a committee-shaped name, and a committee chapter or part. A bare proper-noun heading, or any other heading, is not a signal. Settings with a proceeding class still follow R7.

Correction notice (supersedes the FR20 example in the v2.4 md): a bare proper-noun heading (for example 'QUARRYSIDE') is NOT an identity signal. A classless setting that equals its own leaf is supported under such an ancestor. The v2.4 md listed 'QUARRYSIDE' among ancestors that give qualified; that example was wrong.

FR23: a generic committee name against a neutral leaf (for example 'Meetings' or 'Chairperson') whose part heading names a specific body, listed or committee-shaped, is qualified. This follows from the FR20 ancestor signal together with FR22. Example: 'a committee' under 'HARBOUR COMMITTEE > Meetings' gives qualified_partial; 'a committee' under 'Select committees > Meetings' still gives supported.
T-2 (ruled): any neutral leaf passes a classless setting that has no FR20 ancestor signal. Comparing the leaf's content words is not a cap.

R7 (confirmed for headed settings): the closed FR20 list applies only to classless settings. A setting with a proceeding class (for example 'the Lantern debate') is qualified under an ancestor that names a different proceeding, including a bare proper-noun heading (for example 'ORCHARD' above a 'Lantern debate' leaf).
FR23 (clarified): 'neutral leaf' means any leaf that is not a specific committee. House-level leaves stay under R13 and FR19.

T-3 (ruled): a 'name word' is any word absent from a vocabulary generated from the pinned corpus pack: its headings, path segments and body text. A word counts as a corpus word if it, its plural-folded form, or its -s/-es form appears in that vocabulary. A classless setting against a neutral leaf (any leaf that is not a specific body, the Committee of the whole House, a House-level leaf or a proceeding leaf) is qualified if (a) the leaf shares a word with the setting without equalling it, or (b) the leaf carries a name word the setting lacks. Otherwise the neutral leaf passes, per T-2. A name word never becomes a synthetic proceeding head, so names keep whole-word identity with no plural folding (ruling 4). No hand-written word lists.

T-4 (binding; withdraws the earlier view that role, document and event leaves written in corpus words are neutral). (1) A classless setting that contains a name word is supported only where the leaf or an ancestor names it, meaning the segment contains every content word of the setting as whole words, with no folding. It is qualified everywhere else. (2) 'Neutral' means a leaf that states a rule topic generically (for example 'Time limits', 'General rules', 'Meetings'). A leaf that names a specific role, document, event or stage (for example 'Chairperson', 'The Speaker', a business paper, an opening ceremony, 'Committee stage') is not neutral, so a classless setting that does not equal it is qualified. (3) The overlap clause also catches prefix relations between two corpus words ('second' and 'seconder', 'chair' and 'Chairperson', 'committal' and 'committee'): one word is a prefix of the other with at least 4 letters, or the two share a prefix of at least 5 letters. That counts as overlap without equality, so the result is qualified. Name words are never folded or prefix-matched (ruling 4).

T-4 mechanism (no hand lists): a leaf names a specific role, document, event or stage when (a) it contains the committee head word, or (b) one of its content words is a corpus referent word, or (c) its whole phrase, without determiners, is a corpus referent phrase. Referents are generated from the pinned pack's body text. A referent word occurs at least 5 times and either (i) is preceded by 'the' in at least 50% of occurrences and used as a noun-phrase head (followed by punctuation or a generated function word in at least 50% of occurrences; the function words are the 60 most frequent body words), or (ii) is capitalised mid-sentence in at least 80% of occurrences. A referent phrase (2 or 3 words) occurs at least 5 times and is preceded by 'the' in at least 50% of occurrences. 'The Speaker' and 'Chairperson' are referents; 'Time limits' and 'General rules' are not.

T-3/T-4 (accepted limits): (1) a classless setting that is itself a corpus word may still reach a leaf that shares that word through the proceeding route (for example 'the second' against 'Second ballot'). (2) An everyday word that does not occur in the corpus counts as a name word, so a setting or leaf built on it is qualified unless the path names it, which is over-cautious. (3) The referent signal is statistical. Some generic topic leaves count as specific and become over-cautious (some single generic nouns and some '... of business' topic leaves). Some sparse roles count as neutral (a word used fewer than 5 times, such as 'seconder', is caught only by the prefix clause). (4) Leaves at House level ('Adjournment of the House') name a specific body, so they are qualified against a classless setting. (5) The vocabulary and referent data must be regenerated and pinned whenever the corpus pack changes.
